dateAssessment: Working dates use the session YAML, August 9–21, 1748. Only August is spoken independently. Counting departure as sailing day one places the fifth-day Illoria passage on August 13 and the roughly eighth-day canal approach on August 16; the two canal overnights then reach August 18. The final sea leg is ‘four-ish days’ followed by about half a day upriver. The YAML arrival date is a compatible working date, not an independently verified endpoint; taking that sea estimate as exactly four days would place arrival about a day later. The time extraction therefore remains **compatible**, with the total date-boundary count open. Mirror time is subjective and separate from Wellby’s adventure clock.

watches.summary: Afternoon harbor meeting; later on deck the DM gives about three, two hours before sunset.
Initial sailing description uses setting sunlight; its relation to the later afternoon anchor remains unresolved.
A couple of hours reach sunset; dinner and stories continue into the late evening.
By the next evening the ship reaches the Isle of Folly and turns northwest.
Illoria appears on the fifth morning, correcting an initial fourth-day start.
Around sailing day eight, the canal approach is placed in late afternoon.
The four PCs enter at sunset; Baxter joins in the retrospectively resolved shrinking sequence.
White mist feels like minutes or perhaps an hour; no hunger, thirst or tiredness develops.
Evening pilot arrangements end in sleep; Wellby wakes before dawn the next morning.
Wellby wakes in pre-dawn darkness; magical wind begins the transit before sunrise.
Lake arrival is nine-ish in the morning, after briefly considering ten.
Sunset reveals the sea; Fort Varian docking follows in full darkness, well past sunset.
The ship spends the night at anchor; four PCs emerge as it leaves next morning.
About four days of sailing follow the morning departure; the river arrival watch is unstated.
The upriver approach takes about half a day; departure and arrival watches are unstated.
